chapter: University of Chicago and the Cakewalking Babies
title: University of Chicago and the Cakewalking Babies
summary: After the Navy he came to Chicago on the GI Bill; Steiner and he list the Cakewalking Babies' members.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, I came to the University of Chicago after I got out of the Navy. I got out of the Navy in 1946. And my friend Dan Gerald, who I had played with in Boston and who we had a mutual interest in jazz, he was at the University of Chicago. So I came here under the G.I. Bill of Rights. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. What did you take up at the University? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I took the liberal arts course in the college. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Still thinking of being a musician, possibly? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Oh yes, I was very much interested in that. I wanted to get an education, but I think I was mainly interested in becoming a musician.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was Gerald behind the formation of the jazz group at Chipoga?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, Dan was playing with what members of it were here then. He was here a year or so before I came here. And after I came here, he sort of became interested in other things. And Jack Selden became the drummer.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Jack Selden was from Texas, is that right? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I remember him going back and I corresponded with him years later, but I hadn't heard of him in recent years. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. That is maybe in mid-50s or something. I don't know if we had an exchange or two. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now in 49, you came to, 48 rather, you came to the University. And do you remember who made up the first groups that you played with? Was it then called the Cakewalking Babies?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, it didn't have a name at first. We just sort of thought that was a hot sounding name, so we adopted it. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. It was Bill Price on trumpet and Alan Fredrickson on trombone and myself. And there was a piano player named Paul Jackson and a banjo player named Paul Boeberg and Jack Seldon on drums. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I think that was the regular group. There may have been others who played from time to time.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Then about the time you left, some of the others left too, that is the band more or less broke up about 50, didn't it? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Bill Price kept a group together, but your group had pretty well spread.
